image_description: A close-up, high-resolution shot of the head and upper torso of a Nile crocodile resting on sandy ground. The mouth is slightly open, revealing interlocking teeth. The skin texture is highly detailed, showing rough, bony scutes on the dorsal side and smoother scales near the jawline. The eye is visible with a vertical pupil.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers to a distinct point, consistent with the V-shape of a crocodile rather than the U-shape of an alligator. The head structure appears anatomically correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Teeth are clearly visible. The fourth tooth on the lower jaw appears to fit into a notch on the upper jaw, a key diagnostic feature of crocodiles. The teeth look sharp and conical.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is positioned on top of the skull. The pupil is a vertical slit. The eye surface has a realistic wet sheen and structural integrity.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Nostrils are visible at the anterior end of the snout, correctly placed for a semi-aquatic reptile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows heavy armor plating (scutes) and extends out of frame, implying an elongated form.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture on the back shows distinct, raised, bony plates arranged in rows. The texture is complex and non-repetitive, indicating high fidelity.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Coloration matches the description (olive/brown/grey mix). The texture appears rough and calcified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral surface (belly) is not visible in this angle; the crocodile is lying on its stomach.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are completely occluded by the body and the angle of the shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is outside the frame.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification and rule out hybrid or generic reptile artifacts.
To analyze the micro-texture of the scutes for signs of AI 'smearing' or inconsistent detail resolution.
To ensure the teeth are distinct objects and not fused with the gums or lips, a common AI failure mode.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition between the hard scutes and the softer skin around the jaw. AI often blurs this boundary. Also, verify that the teeth do not 'melt' into the gum line.

metadata.class_label: African crocodile, Nile crocodile, Crocodylus niloticus
